historical_record.description: Built as the Southern District police station, two storeys in concrete, designed by Shea & Shea.
Damaged in the earthquake and fire, then repaired and returned to service without its original corner turret.
Ceased to be the Southern District station when the police department moved to new district headquarters on Valencia Street.

building.completed_conflict: The assessor dates the building to 1903; the city's 2011 survey of Showplace Square and the northeast Mission dates it to 1899.

historic_survey.note: The survey rates the architecture 5 of 5. The 2009 context statement gives the status code 3CB; the 2011 survey data table gives 3CS. California Register criteria cited: 1, 2, 3.
historic_survey.status_code_meaning: California Historical Resource Status Codes: a 1 or 2 means listed or formally determined eligible, a 3 means the survey judged it eligible, a 5 means locally significant, a 6 that it was found ineligible, and a 7 that it was not evaluated.
